rule: A ready-for-review PR requires the local review gate to hold when local review ran; only the workflow script opens a loop-cap draft
description: P3 coupling. `plugin/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements) is the single home of the local review gate and of its one draft exception. The source pin is ONE span carrying both halves of the gate claim: the holding set (`clean`, and `diminishing-returns` once its advisory exit is taken) and the obligation on the rest (any other exit holds nothing and stops that PR, the ready-for-review PR the gate's first sentence names, on every path: workflow script, state machine, or any step outside both). Adding a third holding exit reason inside the sentence, dropping the advisory-exit condition on `diminishing-returns`, rewriting `holds nothing`, or narrowing `on every path` or its list of paths turns the suite red. A consumer in the same file pins the discriminating condition and its obligation as ONE span: if local review ran on the branch, a ready-for-review PR opens only when its last exit reason holds the gate. Dropping the ran-on-the-branch condition, dropping the ready-for-review scope, or keying the gate on an exit reason other than the last one turns the suite red. A second consumer in the same file pins the not-run clause: local review that did not run (not configured, or skipped) neither holds nor blocks the PR, so rewriting a skipped review into a blocker or into a hold turns the suite red. A third consumer in the same file pins the loop-cap draft rule as ONE span carrying its condition and its obligations: at a loop cap, only the workflow script opens the PR as a draft whose body says why and lists open findings; validation still passes; other paths stop. Dropping the loop-cap condition, dropping `only the workflow script`, dropping the draft or either body obligation, dropping the validation clause, or dropping `Other paths stop.` turns the suite red. Two consumers in `plugin/skills/open-plan-pr/SKILL.md` pin the pointers to the canonical section, the step 4 check and a Do Not bullet, each naming `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements); they pin the reference, not the rule, so the skill restates no exit reason and no cap. Deleting a pointer, retargeting its file or section, or dropping the loop-cap draft from the step 4 check or the ready-for-review scope from the Do Not bullet turns the suite red. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these six word sequences exist in these two named files; they claim nothing about meaning and nothing about what the workflow script, the state machine, or an agent actually does. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a meaning inversion around the pinned bytes, such as a later sentence in the section that names a further holding exit reason or a further path allowed to open a draft, is invisible; (2) the pins are whole-file, so moving a pinned sentence out of the PR Requirements section stays green; (3) the rule names no loop cap, so which caps count lives in the engine's cap constants and is not checked here, and agreement between this statement and the engines' own routing tables is not checked either, because a presence pin cannot compare two tables; (4) `that PR` in the source pin and `Other paths` in the loop-cap pin take their meaning from the neighbouring pinned sentences, so a rewrite that keeps each pinned span but reorders the sentences around them is invisible; (5) the Do Not bullet's negation comes from the `## Do Not` heading, not from the pinned sentence, and the heading is unpinned; (6) the `expect_commit` sentence in the skill, by which a caller's local review check stands in for the skill's own, is unpinned; (7) the skill's step 4 cannot tell which caller it runs for, so its loop-cap draft pointer relies on the canonical section to limit the draft to the workflow script; (8) a NEW PR-opening path that never carries a pointer to the canonical section is an absence defect no fixture in this directory can see, per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.

source.pattern: Gate-holding exits: `clean`, and `diminishing-returns` once its advisory exit is taken. Any other exit holds nothing and stops that PR on every path: workflow script, state machine, or any step outside both.

consumers.pattern: Local review gate: if local review ran on the branch, a ready-for-review PR opens only when its last exit reason holds the gate.
Local review that did not run (not configured, or skipped) neither holds nor blocks the PR.
Loop-cap draft: at a loop cap, only the workflow script opens the PR as a draft whose body says why and lists open findings; validation still passes. Other paths stop.
that the local review gate held, local review did not run, or the PR is a loop-cap draft, per `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements)
- open a ready-for-review PR when local review ran on the branch and did not hold the local review gate per `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements)
